options.content: **03 · OQL query over gRPC.** The grpc-go client runs OQL with the `Query` RPC: the server executes it and streams the rows back, up to `gemfire.grpc.query-batch-size` per message. Load comes from `make select-load-test EX=03 SCRIPT=query/steady`, which mixes five queries (the **query** dropdown): `scan`, `range`, `count`, `top` and `key`.

panels.title: At a glance: selected load runs over the time range
Peak queries/s
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Highest queries/s k6 sustained (30-second windows).

panels.title: Peak rows/s
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Highest rows/s the queries returned (30-second windows).

panels.title: Query p50
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Median time of the whole Query call: from sending the request to the last row.

panels.title: Query p99
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. 99th percentile.

panels.title: Failed queries
panels.description: Share of /query calls that failed, from the client's demo_op_latency_seconds{code!="OK"}. It counts every caller (k6, the demo, curl), so it ignores the dropdowns.

panels.title: Query time p50 and p99, by query
panels.description: The whole Query call, as the client timed it (X-GemFire-Micros).

panels.title: Rows/s, by query
panels.description: Rows the queries returned per second. scan and range return about 100 rows each, count one row, top 10 rows, key one row.

panels.title: Per query, over the time range
panels.description: Queries, average rows per query, and the Query call's p50/p99 for the selected runs.

targets.expr: sum by (op) (increase(k6_query_rows_total{client="grpc-go", run=~"$run", op=~"$op"}[$__range])) / sum by (op) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{client="grpc-go", run=~"$run", op=~"$op"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Load test (k6): end-to-end vs. Query call
End-to-end vs. Query call (p50)
panels.description: The gap is the HTTP request around the query: k6 → client and back, JSON encoding.

panels.title: gRPC Query streams (interceptor): every call, the demo's included
Query calls/s by status code
panels.description: From the client's stream interceptor. Errors such as INVALID_ARGUMENT, FAILED_PRECONDITION or UNIMPLEMENTED come from the demo and from curl.

panels.title: QueryResponse messages per call
panels.description: About rows ÷ query-batch-size, and never less than 1: an empty result is still one message.

panels.title: GemFire servers: what the cluster sees
Query executions/s per server
panels.description: CachePerfStats.queryExecutions. On a partitioned region a query runs on every server that hosts its buckets, and each server counts its per-bucket executions too, so this is far higher than queries/s. Use it for the trend and the server1/server2 balance, not as a query count.

panels.title: Average execution time per server
panels.description: CachePerfStats.queryExecutionTime (nanoseconds) ÷ queryExecutions: the average per execution as the server counts them (per bucket on a partitioned region), so it's much shorter than the whole Query call.

panels.title: Partitioned-query messages sent
panels.description: QueryMessages a server sends to the other server, asking it to run the query on its own buckets. The gRPC client talks only to server1, so server1 sends them.
